newsitem.title: GERMANY: Forex moves a normalisation from '95 - German Finmin.
newsitem.headline: Forex moves a normalisation from '95 - German Finmin.

text.p: Recent moves in foreign exchange markets represent a normalisation from the situation prevaling in early 1995 and should be conducive to German growth this year, the German Finance Ministry said on Thursday.

The ministry's comment follows rapid gains in the U.S. dollar against the mark. The dollar climbed to 1.6535/40 to the German unit after data showing that unemployment hit a post-war record in January.

The dollar, which hit an all-time low of 1.3450 marks in March 1995, rose about six percent last month. Some officials in the Group of Seven nations, which will meet on Saturday in Berlin, have expressed concern at the speed of the rise.
In the statement, issued in advance of the G7 meeting, the finance ministry said exchange rates between G7 nations would be discussed within the context of a discussion about world growth.
The ministry said it expected these talks to conclude that current conditions were favourable for continued growth due to the low interest and exchange rates,
The G7 groups Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States.
